metadata.title: The relationship between information literacy and digital self-efficacy in teaching information literacy for new teachers in Lithuania

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study collected primary survey data in Lithuania in 2022 from two teacher-training centres (Vytautas Magnus University and Vilnius University) using simple random sampling within the enrolled student populations. The manuscript reports a sample size calculation and confidence interval (95% confidence level, 5% interval) but does not report the use of any complex survey weights or replicate-weight procedures. Because the analysis is based on structural equation modelling (AMOS) and nonparametric group comparison (Mann–Whitney), the paper does not describe applying sampling weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or any BRR/jackknife scheme. Therefore, weighting variables are not documented for analysts to reproduce; results should be interpreted as associations within the sampled Lithuanian teacher-education populations rather than as fully design-weighted national estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This study does not use ILSA cognitive achievement outcomes with Plausible Values; instead, it models latent constructs from questionnaire items (digital self-efficacy and information literacy components) using SEM. Because the dependent variables are survey-based Likert/self-assessment measures rather than PV-based achievement scores, PV handling is not applicable. The manuscript also does not report a missing-data strategy (e.g., listwise deletion or imputation), which is a reporting gap for reproducibility, even though the paper reports reliability/validity and model fit indices.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Participants were recruited from the two largest teacher-training centres in Lithuania (Vytautas Magnus University and Vilnius University). The analytic sample comprised 191 undergraduate students pursuing teaching qualifications via concurrent/adjacent routes and 214 requalification programme teachers pursuing teaching qualifications via consecutive routes. The paper does not describe additional item-level exclusions (e.g., incomplete questionnaire handling) or any further filtering beyond the two target-group definitions.

main_findings.dataset_used: ICILS 2018 (conceptual framework referenced; study uses Lithuania 2022 teacher survey)
main_findings.target_variable: Digital self-efficacy in teaching information literacy (DSE) — undergraduate students
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ICILS 2018-referenced information literacy components as the conceptual basis (with Lithuania 2022 survey data), the study leveraged information evaluation literacy, information processing literacy, information seeking literacy, and information dissemination literacy to predict digital self-efficacy in teaching information literacy for undergraduate students, finding that information processing and information evaluation had the strongest direct effects (βIP=0.849, βIE=0.834, both p<.001). This indicates that strengthening teachers’ information evaluation and processing capabilities in initial teacher education may be a high-leverage pathway to improve their confidence in teaching information literacy, though the design is correlational and does not establish causality.

main_findings.dataset_used: ICILS 2018 (conceptual framework referenced; study uses Lithuania 2022 teacher survey)
main_findings.target_variable: Digital self-efficacy in teaching information literacy (DSE) — requalification programme teachers
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ICILS 2018-referenced information literacy components as the conceptual basis (with Lithuania 2022 survey data), the study leveraged information evaluation literacy, information processing literacy, information seeking literacy, and information dissemination literacy to predict digital self-efficacy in teaching information literacy for requalification programme teachers, finding that information evaluation and information processing were the strongest predictors (βIE=0.821, βIP=0.774, both p<.001). This indicates that professional requalification programmes should prioritize training that improves evaluation and processing of information to raise teachers’ self-efficacy for teaching information literacy, while noting that the SEM results reflect associations among latent constructs rather than causal effects.

main_findings.dataset_used: Lithuania 2022 teacher survey (undergraduate vs requalification programme)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Mann–Whitney: DSE1 (internet search abilities) U=6944.00, p=.019; DSE6 (netiquette, privacy, copyright) U=7044.50, p=.034. Descriptives: undergraduate DSE2 mean=4.26 (SD=.096) vs requalification DSE2 mean=4.47 (SD=.797); DSE1 mean=3.21 (SD=.904) vs 3.36 (SD=.911); DSE6 mean=4.26 (SD=.936) vs 4.45 (SD=.825).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using Lithuania 2022 survey the study compared undergraduate students and requalification programme teachers on perceived digital self-efficacy in teaching information literacy, finding statistically significant higher scores for requalification teachers on internet search abilities (DSE1) and on netiquette/privacy/copyright (DSE6). This indicates that requalification pathways may be associated with stronger self-efficacy in specific information-literacy teaching subskills, suggesting that initial teacher education may need targeted support in these areas to close the confidence gap.

data.outcome_summary: The study uses Lithuania 2022 survey data (N=405) from two teacher-training groups—191 undergraduate students and 214 requalification programme teachers—to examine how perceived information literacy components relate to digital self-efficacy in teaching information literacy. Information literacy is operationalized via IL-HUMASS subcomponents (information seeking, evaluation, processing, dissemination) and digital self-efficacy via DSE items (DSE1–DSE6). Using SEM in AMOS, all four information literacy components show positive direct effects on DSE in both groups, with the strongest standardized paths from information evaluation and information processing (undergraduates: βIE=0.834, βIP=0.849; requalification teachers: βIE=0.821, βIP=0.774; all p<.01). Group comparisons via Mann–Whitney indicate requalification teachers score higher on internet search abilities and netiquette/privacy/copyright. Limitations include the absence of a documented missing-data strategy and the correlational nature of SEM (no causal identification).
